text:
cheng: heads-up — hit a weird perf regression when running the paged/Flash-attn path on SM90 with CUDA 12.3. baseline on SM86 (cuda 11.8) used the CUDA fused kernel and was ~15% faster for our 2–8 token prefix case.

cheng: quick numbers from my local microbench (single-GPU, 1k warm iters then avg 200 iters):
- SM86 (fused CUDA): 1.12 ms / token (B=1, seq=1024)
- SM90 (triton-paged variant): 1.34 ms / token (B=1, seq=1024)
- SM90 (force-cuda fallback): 1.20 ms / token

jordan: can you repro on dedicated infra (non-devbox)? looks like triton kernel on SM90 is doing extra device<->host shuffles or worse launch overhead. do you have nvtx traces?

cheng: yes repros on dedicated. attached quick NVTX excerpt (stripped):
```
[NVTX] 0. profiler: run 0
[NVTX] 1. flash_paged_attention_kernel (triton): 452 us
[NVTX] 2. memcpy_async H2D staging: 60 us
[NVTX] 3. kernel launch overheads: 18 us (per-chunk)
```
seems like paged path introduces host staging for certain KV pages, and with small B/long seq the per-chunk launch + memcpy adds up.

sam: hmm. two quick ideas: 1) try forcing CUDA kernels to isolate Triton overhead (env var REDWOOD_FORCE_CUDA_KERNELS=1 in our runtime). 2) check batching heuristic: if the scheduler is splitting into many micro-batches because seq-length distribution is wide, launch overhead multiplies.

cheng: did (1). forced CUDA kernels -> 1.20 ms (as above). So Triton path is the main regression. Also ran our batching dump and found many small micro-batches for requests with mixed seq lengths (mostly 128/1024 mix). heuristics are still tuned for SM86 behavior.

maria: are KV pages being pinned/unpinned differently on newer drivers/arch? paged attention uses host staging when memory pressure spikes — that will surface as H2D memcpy spikes. did you try toggling paged_kv_prefetch?

ivan: quick experiment: try enabling contiguous-kv branch (allocs contiguous mmap to avoid scatter) or set paged_kv_prefetch=2 to prefetch hot pages into device before step. should reduce H2D during critical path.

cheng: tried paged_kv_prefetch=2. results:
- SM90 (triton, prefetch=2): 1.28 ms
- SM90 (triton, prefetch=4): 1.24 ms
so helps but still ~10% behind SM86 fused kernel. interestingly, prefetch reduces memcpy variance but doesn't remove chunk launch penalty completely.

perf-bot: automated-run: cross-arch-attn-compat:
- job 1845679: sm86-cuda11.8:fused -> baseline throughputs saved
- job 1845680: sm90-cuda12.3:triton-paged -> -12.5% p50 throughput vs baseline
- job 1845681: sm90-cuda12.3:cuda-fallback -> -7.1% p50 vs baseline
(see /bench/reports/18456*.html)

jordan: sounds like multiple levers: (A) Triton kernel launch pattern for paged attention is suboptimal on SM90 (maybe new SM90 launch cost or nvcc codegen) (B) KV prefetch reduces memcpy but not launch overhead (C) batching heuristics create too many micro-launches for mixed seq workloads.

sam: agree. short plan: 1) bisect Triton change set that touches flash_paged kernel for SM90 (maybe kernel grid sizing changed). 2) add a quick runtime switch to increase chunk-size on SM90 to amortize launch cost. 3) tune batching heuristics to coalesce small seqs into same target so fewer launches.

cheng: created issue + PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/5784. PR will add env REDWOOD_CHUNK_MIN_TOKENS and a dev flag to prefer CUDA-fallback for critical routes.

maria: also add a small test to evict/prefetch KV pages and assert memcpy H2D < X ms to catch regressions on CI.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: attn-kernel-sm90-hotfix -> staging at 2028-04-12T15:40Z :rocket:

jordan: nice work. let's pair for 30m tomorrow to triage the Triton launch cost; assign folks from perf and runtime. @cheng can you drop the exact failing nvprof trace in the issue? :thumbsup:

cheng: will upload full nvprof + synthetic bench logs to the issue. thanks all.
